+## Installation and Setup
+
+Complete the following steps to install the setup BigCloneEval.
+
+Alternatively, download the VM version of BigCloneEval to have a pre-configured
+environment. Username: `bce`, password: `clones`.
+
+VM available in VMWare format at: https://1drv.ms/u/s!AhXbM6MKt_yLj_42w4Y-l5isPPiOOw?e=SIS5yW
+
+The VM was created with VMWare Player Workstation, which is free for personal and educational
+purposes: https://www.vmware.com/products/workstation-player.html.
+
+### Step 1: Get the latest version of BigCloneEval
+
+BigCloneEval is available as a github repository.  The latest version can be retrieved
+using the following git command:
+```
+git clone https://github.com/jeffsvajlenko/BigCloneEval
+```
+
+### Step 2: Get the latest version of BigCloneBench
+
+Direct link: https://1drv.ms/u/s!AhXbM6MKt_yLj_NwwVacvUzmi6uorA?e=eMu0P4
+
+Extract the contents of BigCloneBench (BigCloneBench_BCEvalVersion.tar.gz) into the
+'bigclonebenchdb' directory of the BigCloneEval distribution.
+
+To manually view this database, use h2database: http://h2database.com/html/main.html.
+
+### Step 3: Get the latest version of IJaDataset
+
+Direct link: https://1drv.ms/u/s!AhXbM6MKt_yLj_N15CewgjM7Y8NLKA?e=cScoRJ
+
+Extract the contents of IJaDataset (IJaDataset_BCEvalVersion.tar.gz) into the 'ijadataset'
+directory of the BigCloneEval distribution.
+
+This should create a directory 'ijadataset/bcb_reduced/' which contains one sub-directory
+per functionality in BigCloneBench.
+
+### Step 4: Build the source code.
+
+From the root directory, run `make`.
+
+### Step 5: Initialize the tools database
+
+From the `commands/` directory, execute the `init` script.  This will initialize the tools
+database.
+
+
+## Using BigCloneEval
+
+The following documents the usage of BigCloneEval.  Please also see the demonstration
+video on the BigCloneEval webpage.
+
+### Experimental Process
+
+To evaluate the recall of a clone detection tool you must complete the following steps:
+
+1. Register the clone detection tool with BigCloneEval.
+2. Detect clones in IJaDataset using the clone detection tool.
+3. Import the detected clones into BigCloneEval.
+4. Configure and execution the evaluation experiment.
+
+These steps are performed using BigCloneEval's commands, which are located in the command/
+directory as scripts.  These scripts must be executed from within the command directory
+(the command directory must be the working directory).
+
+In the next section we outline the available commands.  Then we discuss how each step can
+be performed in detail.  Then we include specific documentation for each command.
+
+### Commands Summary
+
+The commands are available in the `commands/` directory, and should be executed from that
+directory.  Executing the commands with the `-h` flag will show their parameters.
+The special `bcb` command can execute all other commands and provide a usage help. Run
+`./bcb help` to get the following overview:
+
+```
+Usage: bcb COMMAND
+The big clone bench tool
+Commands:
+  clearClones     Removes the imported clones for the specified registered tool.
+  countClones     Count the number of clones that have been imported for the
+                    tool.
+  deleteTool      Deletes a tool, specified by its ID, from the framework. Also
+                    removes any imported clones for this tool.
+  detectClones    Executes the clone detection tool for IJaDataset in an
+                    automated procedure. Requires a script that configures and
+                    executes the tool, and the scalability limits of the tool
+                    in terms of the maximum input size measured in source
+                    files. Used deterministic input partitioning to overcome
+                    scalability limits. Optional, clone detection can be
+                    performed manually if desired.
+  evaluateRecall  Measures the recall of the clones given. Highly configureable.
+                    Summarizes recall per clone type, per inter vs
+                    intra-project clones, per functionality in BigCloneBench
+                    and for different syntactical similarity regions in the
+                    output tool evaluation report.
+  evaluateTool    Measures the recall of the specific tool based on the clones
+                    imported for it. Highly configureable, including using
+                    custom clone-matching algorithms. Summarizes recall per
+                    clone type, per inter vs intra-project clones, per
+                    functionality in BigCloneBenchand for different syntactical
+                    similarity regions in the output tool evaluation report.
+  importClones    Imports the clones detected by a tool in IJaDataset into the
+                    framework for evaluation. Clones are provided as clone
+                    pairs in a simple CSV file. See documentation below for the
+                    expected format.
+  init            This command initializes the tools database. It is used on
+                    first-time setup. It can also be used to restore the tools
+                    database to its original condition. This will delete any
+                    tools, and their clones, from the database, and restart the
+                    ID increment to 1.
+                  This may take some time to execute as the database is
+                    compacted.
+  listTools       Lists the tools registered in the database. Including their
+                    ID, name and description.
+  partitionInput  partitions the files from the input directory to the output
+                    directory.
+  registerTool    Registers a clone detection tool with the framework. Requires
+                    a name and description of the tool, which is stored in the
+                    tools database. Returns a unique identifier for the tool
+                    for indicating the target tool for the other commands. Name
+                    and description are for reference by the user.
+  help            Displays help information about the specified command
+```
+		
+### Step 1: Register Tool
+
+First the tool must be registered to the framework.  This is done by the registerTool
+command, which requires a name and description of the tool.  The intention is for the user
+to use the name field to record the name and version of the tool, and the description to
+denote the configuration used in the detection experiment.  These are stored for later
+reference by the user.  A unique identifier is output for the user to refer to this tool
+in the latter steps.
+
+
+### Step 2: Clone Detection
+
+Next the tool must be executed for IJaDataset.  This can be done manually or using our 
+detectClones command.  Use the method which is easiest for your tool.
+
+#### Manually
+You must execute the tool for each subdirectory in `ijadataset/bcb_sample`.  For example,
+you must execute the tool for `ijadataset/bcb_sample/2` and `ijadataset/bcb_sample/3`,
+etc.  Each sub-directory is the files from the full IJaDataset that contain clones of one
+of the functionalities in BigCloneBench.
+
+Some of these sub-directories may contain too many source files for the scalability
+constraints of some tools, particularly those that require significant memory.  In this
+case the partitionInput command can be used to split these inputs into a number of smaller
+inputs given a maximum number of files the tool can reliably handle.
+
+#### Automatically
+To use the automatic clone detection procedure, a script must be provided that configures
+and executes the tool.  On Linux and OSX this is expected to be a bash script, and it
+executed using `bash -c /path/to/script/ /path/to/clone/detection/input/`.  On Windows,
+this is expected to be a command script, and is executed using
+`cmd.exe /c C:\path\to\script\ C:\path\to\clone\detection\input\`.
+
+The script is expected to take as a parameter a directory which contains source code
+(possibly in sub-directories) for clone detection to be executed on.  The script should
+configure and execute the tool, and output the detected clones to stdout.  The script
+should terminate with an exit code of 0 if it was successful, or non-zero if it failed.
+The tool should not output anything to stdout except for the detected clones.  Ideally,
+the clones should be output in the format expected by the `importClones` command (see the
+next step), although any output is supported.  
+
+The `sample/` directory contains the `nicadRunner` as an example bash script targeting
+Linux/OSX, and and `iclonesRunner.cmd` command script targeting Windows.  Note that these
+scripts won't run as is, and will require downloading and installing the clone detection
+tools, and modifying the runner to work with your computer's environment.
+
+The `detectClones` command takes this script as input, the maximum files the tool can handle
+without scalability issues on the available hardware, and a scratch directory to use in
+case input partitioning is required for scalability issues (otherwise the OS tmp directory
+is used).
+
+`detectClones` then executes the script with each sub-directory in `ijadatset/bcb_sample/`
+as input, using input partitioning on the sub-directories that exceed the tool's indicated
+scalability constraints.  The output from each execution is concatenated into a final
+output file.
+
+Note that due to the nature of how we reduced IJaDataset, and how input partitioning
+works, the final output may contain some duplicated clones (not the fault of the tool
+itself).  These can be trimmed from the output if desired, but will not affect the
+evaluation results.
+
+### Step 3: Import Clones
+
+The next step is to import the clones, which is done using the `importClones` command.  This
+takes the ID of the registered tool, and a file containing the clones.  The `importClones`
+command expects the clones to be formatted in a simple CSV file, where each line specifies
+one clone pair in the following format:
+
+```
+cf1_subdirectory,cf1_filename,cf1_startline,cf1_endline,cf2_subdirectory,cf2_filename,cf2_endline
+```
+
+For example:
+
+```
+selected,102353.java,10,20,default,356923.java,20,30
+sample,DownloadWebpage.java,20,50,selected,10234,356123.java,30,50
+```
+
+Where `cf#_subdirectory,cf#_filename,cf#_startline,cf#_endline` specifies one of the code
+fragments.  And the order of the code fragments in the clone pair does not matter.
+
+`cf#_subdirectory` is the sub-directory of IJaDataset the source file is found in.
+IJaDataset has three subdirectories: `selected`, `default` and `sample`.  For example,
+sub-input `ijadataset/bcb_sample/2` contains a `selected`, `default` and `sample`
+directory.  The meaning behind the sub-directories is not important, but it needs to be
+specified to fully resolve the source file.
+
+If your tool outputs clone classes, they need to be converted into clone pairs for this
+format.
+
+### Step 4: Execute evaluation.
+
+The evaluate command is used to measure the recall of the clone detection tool for
+BigCloneBench based on its imported clones.  This takes the ID of the tool, a file to
+output the tool evaluation report to, and a number of configuration options for
+customizing the recall evaluation experiment.
+
+#### Clone Matcher
+A clone matcher must be specified.  This is the algorithm used to determine if a reference
+clone in the benchmark is sufficiently captured by a candidate clone reported by the tool
+for the reference clone to be considered as detected by the candidate tool.
+
+BigCloneEval includes our coverage-based clone matching algorithm.  More details are
+provided below in the Command Documentation section.  This is implemented in a plugin
+architecture such that users can implement their own clone matching algorithm using our
+existing algorithm as a template.
+
+The clone matcher to be used is specified by name, including a parameter string, when 
+the evaluate command is used.
+
+#### Reference Clone Constraints
+A number of configuration parameters place constraints on which reference clones are
+considered when measuring recall.  The following constraints are available:
+
+ - minimum and/or maximum clone size in tokens, original source lines, and/or pretty-printed source lines
+ - minimum confidence
+ - minimum judges
+
+The clone size constraints makes it easy to set a standard clone size for the experiment
+and appropriately and fairly configure your candidate tools for their benchmark
+experiment.  Clone size constraints are available in the major ways in which clone size
+is typically measured.
+
+The minimum judges constraint selects only those clones whose code fragments (functions)
+have been examined by a minimum number of judges.  Each code fragment has been inspected
+for the functionality of the clone by at least one judge.  Some have been examined by
+multiple judges in order to measure the accuracy of the judging.  This way you can select
+just those examined by some number of judges.  Only a small portion has been examined by
+multiple judges currently.  In future we hope to have the entire benchmark examined by
+multiple judges.
+
+Similar to the minimum judges, the minimum confidence is the minimum agreement when
+multiple judges are used.  This is, for both code fragments, the minimum difference in
+true positive vs false positive votes by the judges.  Currently a small portion of the
+data has been seen by more than two judges, where this constraint is relevant.
+
+#### Similarity Type
+The user can specify how the syntactical similarity of the reference clones should be
+measured.  BigCloneBench includes syntactical similarity measured both by line and by
+token after Type-1 and Type-2 normalizations.  This includes a strict pretty-printing,
+the removal of comments, blind identifier renaming and literal abstraction.  Similarity
+is measured as the minimum ratio of the lines or tokens one code fragment in the clone
+pair shares with the other.  Shared lines or tokens are identified with the diff algorithm
+which considers the order of the lines or tokens.
+
+Syntactical similarity for the experimetn can then be measured by line, by token, by the
+average of the line and token measures, or by both (using the smaller of the two).
+
+We reccomend using `BOTH` as it is the most fair option when comparing token and
+line-based tools without bias.  This is the setting we use in our studies, and when
+reporting the clone demographics of BigCloneBench
+
+#### Minimum Similarity
+You can also specify the minimum syntactical clone similarity of clones to consider.  By
+default, the evaluation considers the full scope of syntactical similarity, 0% to 100%.
+However, most tools are syntax-based, and will have none or near-zero detection much
+below their configured detection threshold.  So some execution time can be saved by
+omitting the reporting of recall for these clones.  The minimum similarity to measure
+recall to must be specified as a multiple of 5.
+
+BigCloneBench divides Type-3 and Type-4 clones by their syntactical similarity into four
+categories:
+
+Very-Strongly Type-3   : Clones with 90% (inclsuive) to 100% (exclusive) shared syntax.
+Strongly Type-3        : Clones with 70% (inclsuive) to  90% (exclusive) shared syntax.
+Moderately Type-3      : Clones with 50% (inclsuive) to  70% (exclusive) shared syntax.
+Weakly Type-3 / Type-4 : Clones with  0% (inclsuive) to  50% (exclusive) shared syntax.
+
+These are canonical categories for BigCloneBench, but evaluate also reports recall for
+every lower threshold and range of syntactical similarity (in 5% granularity).
+
+Most syntax-based Type-3 tools operate mostly in the Very-Stringly and Strongly
+categories.  AST and PDG type tools may have some recall in the moderately Type-3 category
+as well, but not usually significant.
+
+If time allows, it is best to run for full range.  However, executing for a minimum
+similarity of 50% is sufficient for most tools, as they have 0% or near-0% for the Weakly
+Type-3 / Type-4 category, and often similar for the Moderately Type-3.
+
+#### Reccomended Settings
+The reccomended settings are as follows:
+
+similarity type = both line and token (smaller measure)
+minimum clone size in original source lines = 6 lines
+minimum clone size in pretty-printed source lines = 6 lines
+minimum clone size in tokens = 50 tokens
+clone-matcher: Coverage clone matcher with 70% coverage threshold
+
+These correspond to the settings we have used in our previous studies.
+
+#### Tool Evaluation Report
+
+The tool evaluation report sumamrizes recall from a number of perspectives.
+
+Recall is reported per clone type.  Including Type-1, Type-2, Type-3 and Type-4.  The
+recall for Type-2 is reported for different common definitions of Type-2.  Since there is
+no agreed upon minimum similarity of a Type-3 clone, the Type-3 and Type-4 clones are
+split into a number of categories.  Note that sine all of the clones are semantic clones
+(implement a shared functionality), those which do not meet the Type-3 definition are 
+Type-4 clones.  We summarize the per-clone-type categories below:
+
+ - **Type-1**: Recall for the Type-1 clones.
+ - **Type-2**: Recall for all Type-2 clones (most generous definition).
+ - **Type-2 (blind)**: Type-2 clones which don't have a 1:1 mapping of identifier names.
+ - **Type-2 (consistent)**: Type-2 clones which have a 1:1 mapping of identifier names.
+ - **Very-Strongly Type-3**: Clones with sytnactical similarity in range [90,100).
+ - **Strongly Type-3**: Clones with sytnactical similarity in range [70,90)
+ - **Moderately Type-3**: Clones with syntactical similarity in range [50,70)
+ - **Weakly Type-3 or Type-4**: Clones with syntactical similarity in range [0,50)
+	
+The categories assume that Type-4 clones share less than 50% of their syntax.  Most Type-3
+clone detectors should have good recall in the Very-Strongly Type-3 range.  Very good
+Type-3 detectors also have good recall in the Strongly Type-3 while maintaining good
+precision.  It is expected that Moderately Type-3 clones are outside the scope of syntax
+based clone detection approaches, unless precision is significantly compromised.  Other
+techniques that do not rely so much on the syntax of the clone may perform better in this
+range.  The weakly Type-3/Type-4 clones are probably outside the scope of most or all
+clone detection techniques.
+
+Recall is also reported for Type-3/Type-4 clones in different syntactical similarity
+ranges.  It is reported for each range at a granularity of 5%: [0,5), [5,10), etc.  It is
+also reported for each minimum syntactical similarity at a granularity fo 5%: [0,100),
+[5,100), [10,100), etc.
+
+Recall is reported for all clones, for just the inter-project clones, and for just the
+intra-project clones.  Recall can then be compared for these different contexts.
+
+Recall is also reported for all clones, and then also the clones of each individual
+functionality in BigCloneBench.
+
+The evaluation report summarizes the number of reference clones considered in each
+measurement.
+
+The evaluation report documents the version of BigCloneEval and BigCloneBench used to
+create it for future reference.
+
+## Command Documentation
+
+### init
+```
+Usage: bcb init [-hV]
+This command initializes the tools database. It is used on first-time setup. It
+can also be used to restore the tools database to its original condition. This
+will delete any tools, and their clones, from the database, and restart the ID
+increment to 1.
+This may take some time to execute as the database is compacted.
+  -h, --help      Show this help message and exit.
+  -V, --version   Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./init
+```
+
+### registerTool
+```
+Usage: bcb registerTool [-hV] -d=<string> -n=<string>
+Registers a clone detection tool with the framework. Requires a name and
+description of the tool, which is stored in the tools database. Returns a
+unique identifier for the tool for indicating the target tool for the other
+commands. Name and description are for reference by the user.
+  -d, --description=<string>
+                        A description for the tool.  Use quotes to allow spaces
+                          and special characters.
+  -h, --help            Show this help message and exit.
+  -n, --name=<string>   A name for the tool.  Use quotes to allow spaces and
+                          special characters.
+  -V, --version         Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./registerTool -n "NiCad" -d "Default configuration"
+  2
+```
+
+### listTools
+```
+Usage: bcb listTools [-hV]
+Lists the tools registered in the database. Including their ID, name and
+description.
+  -h, --help      Show this help message and exit.
+  -V, --version   Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./listTools
+  1
+  NiCad
+  MyNiCadExecution
+
+  2
+  NiCad
+  Default
+```
+
+### detectClones
+```
+Usage: bcb detectClones [-hnV] -m=<int> -o=<PATH> -r=<PATH> [-s=<PATH>]
+Executes the clone detection tool for IJaDataset in an automated procedure.
+Requires a script that configures and executes the tool, and the scalability
+limits of the tool in terms of the maximum input size measured in source files.
+Used deterministic input partitioning to overcome scalability limits. Optional,
+clone detection can be performed manually if desired.
+  -h, --help             Show this help message and exit.
+  -m, --mf, --max-files=<int>
+                         Maximum files in each output subset (pair of
+                           partitions).
+  -n, --nc, --no-clean   Does not clean up scratch data. For
+                           diagnosis/correction. See documentation. Need to
+                           specify custom scratch directory for this.
+  -o, --output=<PATH>    File to write the report to.
+  -r, --tr, --tool-runner=<PATH>
+                         Path to the tool runner executable.
+  -s, --sd, --scratch-directory=<PATH>
+                         Directory to be used as scratch space. Default is
+                           system tmp directory. Can not already exist.
+  -V, --version          Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./detectClones -tr ~/NiCadRunner -o ~/clones -mf 10000
+```
+
+### importClones
+```
+Usage: bcb importClones [-hV] -c=<FILE> -t=<ID>
+Imports the clones detected by a tool in IJaDataset into the framework for
+evaluation. Clones are provided as clone pairs in a simple CSV file. See
+documentation below for the expected format.
+  -c, --clones=<FILE>   File containing the detected clones.
+  -h, --help            Show this help message and exit.
+  -t, --tool=<ID>       The ID of the tool.
+  -V, --version         Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./importClones -t 2  -c ~/clones
+```
+
+### deleteTool
+```
+Usage: bcb deleteTool [-hV] -t=<ID>
+Deletes a tool, specified by its ID, from the framework. Also removes any
+imported clones for this tool.
+  -h, --help        Show this help message and exit.
+  -t, --tool=<ID>   The ID of the tool.
+  -V, --version     Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./deleteTool -t 2
+```
+
+### clearClones
+```
+Usage: bcb clearClones [-hV] -t=<ID>
+Removes the imported clones for the specified registered tool.
+  -h, --help        Show this help message and exit.
+  -t, --tool=<ID>   The ID of the tool.
+  -V, --version     Print version information and exit.
+```
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./clearClones -t 2
+```
+
+### evaluate
+```
+Usage: bcb evaluateTool [-hV] [-j=<int>] [-m=<MATCHER>] [--mal=<int>]
+                        [--map=<int>] [--mat=<int>] [--mic=<int>] [--mil=<int>]
+                        [--mip=<int>] [--mit=<int>] -o=<PATH> [-s=<int>]
+                        [--st=<STR>] -t=<ID>
+Measures the recall of the specific tool based on the clones imported for it.
+Highly configureable, including using custom clone-matching algorithms.
+Summarizes recall per clone type, per inter vs intra-project clones, per
+functionality in BigCloneBenchand for different syntactical similarity regions
+in the output tool evaluation report.
+  -h, --help                Show this help message and exit.
+  -j, --mij, --minimum-judges=<int>
+                            Minimum number of judges.
+  -m, --matcher=<MATCHER>   Specify the clone matcher. See documentation for
+                              configuration strings. Default is
+                              coverage-matcher with 70% coverage threshold.
+      --mal, --max-lines, --maximum-lines=<int>
+                            Maximum clone size in original lines.
+      --map, --max-pretty, --maximum-pretty=<int>
+                            Maximum clone size in pretty-printed lines.
+      --mat, --max-tokens, --maximum-tokens=<int>
+                            Maximum clone size in tokens.
+      --mic, --minimum-confidence=<int>
+                            Minimum confidence.
+      --mil, --min-lines, --minimum-lines=<int>
+                            Minimum clone size in original lines.
+      --mip, --min-pretty, --minimum-pretty=<int>
+                            Minimum clone size in pretty-printed lines.
+      --mit, --min-tokens, --minimum-tokens=<int>
+                            Minimum clone size in tokens.
+  -o, --output=<PATH>       File to write the report to.
+  -s, --mis, --minimum-similarity=<int>
+                            Minimum clone similarity to evaluate down to.
+      --st, --similarity-type=<STR>
+                            How to measure similarity. One of TOKEN, LINE,
+                              BOTH, AVG. Defaults to BOTH
+  -t, --tool=<ID>           The ID of the tool.
+  -V, --version             Print version information and exit.
+```
+
+#### Clone Matchers:
+
+##### Coverage Matcher
+Requires the tool to report a candidate clone that covers a certain ratio of the
+reference clone for the reference clone to be considered detected.  Takes one or three
+parameters.  The first parameter is the coverage ratio.  We recommend a 0.70 coverage
+ratio.
+	
+Optionally, the user can put a constraint on how far outside of the clone the
+candidate clone can extend while still being considered a match.  Since BigCloneBench
+has function clones, it is not desirable for the tool to report clones that extend 
+significant beyond the boundary of the clone.  The user can specify a tolerance on
+the extension beyond the boundary of the reference clone by a number of original
+source lines, or a ratio of the size of the clone itself.
+	
+Examples:
+	
+ - `CoverageMatcher 0.7`:
+			The candidate clone must cover 70% of the reference clone by line.  The
+			candidate clone can extend indefinitely beyond the boundaries of the reference
+			clone without punishment.
+- `CoverageMatcher 0.7 line 2`:
+			The candidate clone must cover 70% of the reference clone by line.  If the
+			candidate clone extends 2 line beyond the boundary of the reference clone (by
+			either code fragment) then the candidate clone is rejected as a match.
+- `CoverageMatcher 0.7 ratio 0.20`
+			The candidate clone must cover 70% of the reference clone by line.  If the
+			candidate clone extends 20% beyond the boundary of the reference clone, by
+			each code fragment's size in lines, then the candidate clone is rejected as a
+			match.
+			
+See the source file `src/cloneMatchingAlgorithm/CoverageMatcher.java` for more details.
+
+
+##### Custom Clone Matcher
+To provide your own clone matcher, create a class implementing the CloneMatcher
+	interface.  Your custom clone matcher must be in the 'cloneMatchingAlgorithms'
+	package, and on the classpath.  Ideally, install your compiled .class in the
+	'bin/cloneMatchingAlgorithms' directory.  The clone matchers are discovered by
+	reflection at runtime.  Your custom clone matcher must have a constructor which takes
+	an long as its first parameter and a string as it second parameter.  The long is the
+	ID of the tool being evaluated, and the string is the configuration string specified
+	in the execution of evaluate.  You specify your clone matcher as such when executing
+	the evaluate command:
+	
+`-m "MyCloneMatcher arg1 arg2 arg3"`
+	
+The constructor of your clone matcher will be called with the ID of the tool, and then
+	"arg1 arg2 arg3" as the configuration string.
+	
+Your clone matcher implements the `isDetected(Clone clone)` method.  It should check if
+	the specified reference clone was detected using a query over the tool's clone table.
+	
+The tool's clone table will be named: `tool_$ID$_clones`, where `$ID$` is the ID of the
+	tool.  The clone table has fields: `type1`, `name1`, `startline1`, `endline1`, `type2`, `name2`,
+	`startline2`, `endline2`.  Where the start/end lines are integers, and the other
+	parameters are strings (varchar).
+	
+This is in the tools DB, which a connection to this database is available by the
+	`ToolsDB` class.
+	
+Your clone matcher should check both orderings of the reference clone's code fragments
+	as they may be reversed in the tool's detected clones.
+	
+See the existing `CoverageMatcher` as a template.
+	
+BigCloneEval is distributed as an eclipse project.  So the easiest way to develop
+	your own clone matcher is to open BigCloneEval as an eclipse Java project and
+	develop your code from there.
+
+Example:
+```
+  $ ./evaluate -t 3 -o ~/report -st both -m Coverage "CoverageMatcher 0.7 ratio 0.2" -mis 50 -mil 10 -mip 10 -mit 50
+```

+# NiCad Type 3-2 (near-miss renamed) clone configuration parameters
+# J.R. Cordy, Queen's University, May 2010 (revised Jan 2012)
+#
+# NiCad configuration to find type 3-2 (near-miss blind renamed) clone pairs only
+#
+
+# Maximum near-miss difference threshold we are interested in (0.n)
+# For type 3-2 clones, up to 30% different lines allowed 
+
+threshold=0.3
+
+# Sizes of clones we are interested in, in pretty-printed lines
+# Change if you prefer 
+
+minsize=10
+maxsize=10000
+
+# Custom pre-transformation to be applied to potential clones (none, transformname)
+# For traditional type 3-2 clones, no pre-transformation
+
+transform=none
+
+# Kind of renaming to be applied (none, blind, consistent)
+# For traditional type 3-2 clones, blind renaming
+
+rename=blind
+
+# Kind of filtering to be applied (none, nonterminal ...)
+# For traditional type 3-2 clones, no filtering
+
+filter=none
+
+# Kind of abstraction to be applied (none, nonterminal ...)
+# For traditional type 3-2 clones, no abstraction
+
+abstract=literal
+
+# Custom contextual normalizer to be applied to potential clones (none, normname)
+# For traditional type 3-2 clones, no normalization
+
+normalize=none
+
+# Cluster clone pairs into classes
+# Change to yes if desired
+

+#!/bin/bash
+
+# This tool runner works with the myconfig.cfg nicad configuration file included
+# You will need to modify the hard-coded installation below before running
+# Test this out on one of the IJaDataset directories (such as 11/) to test and 
+# see that clones are detected and output in the correct format for BigCloneEval
+# as specified in the readme.
+
+ulimit -s hard
+
+root=`dirname $1`
+dir=`basename $1`
+path=$root/$dir
+
+# Go to NiCad installation directory
+cd /home/jeff/Applications/NiCad-4.0/
+
+# Execute NiCad, Suppress Output
+./nicad4 functions java "$path" myconfig > /dev/null 2> /dev/null
+
+# Convert Detected Clones Into BigCloneEval Format
+#java -jar Convert.jar ${path}_functions-blind-abstract-clones/${dir}_functions-blind-abstract-clones-0.30.xml 2> /dev/null
+
+cat ${path}_functions-blind-abstract-clones/${dir}_functions-blind-abstract-clones-0.30.xml | sed 's$<source file="$$g' | sed 's$" startline="$,$g' | sed 's$" endline="$,$g' | sed 's$" pcid=.*"></source>$$g' | sed 's$<clone nlines=.*$$g' | sed 's$</clone>.*$$g' | sed 's$</clones>$$g' |sed 's$<clones>$$g' | sed 's$<cloneinfo.*$$g' | sed 's$<systeminfo.*$$g' | sed 's$<runinfo.*$$g' | sed '/^$/d' | paste -d ',' - - | sed "s#${path}/##g" | sed 's#/#,#g'
+
+# Cleanup
+rm -rf ${path}_functions-blind-abstract-clones > /dev/null 2> /dev/null
+rm ${path}_functions-blind-abstract.xml > /dev/null 2> /dev/null
+rm ${path}_functions-clones*.log > /dev/null 2> /dev/null
+rm ${path}_functions-blind.xml > /dev/null 2> /dev/null
+rm ${path}_functions.xml > /dev/null 2> /dev/null

+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Verifies that all JNorm, ONorm and source files can be parsed by TXL for NiCad.
+# Run inside the Docker container after the pipeline has produced the work/ output.
+#
+# - jnorm-soot        jimple files  (/app/work/jnorm-soot)
+# - jnorm-soot-agg    jimple files  (/app/work/jnorm-soot-agg)
+# - jnorm-sootup      jimple files  (/app/work/jnorm-sootup)
+# - jnorm-sootup-agg  jimple files (/app/work/jnorm-sootup-agg)
+# - onorm             tac files     (/app/work/onorm)
+# - onorm-agg         tac files     (/app/work/onorm-agg)
+# - source            java files    (/app/work/source)
+#
+# Requires: find, xargs, nproc, /usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/
+set -eu
+
+JIMPLE_PARSER="/usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/jimple-extract-functions.x"
+TAC_PARSER="/usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/tac-extract-functions.x"
+JAVA_PARSER="/usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/java-extract-functions.x"
+
+if [ ! -f /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max ]; then
+  MAX_PROCS=$(nproc)
+else
+  QUOTA=$(awk '{print $1}' /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max)
+  PERIOD=$(awk '{print $2}' /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max)
+  if [ "$QUOTA" = "max" ]; then
+    MAX_PROCS=$(nproc)
+  else
+    MAX_PROCS=$(( QUOTA / PERIOD ))
+    [ "$MAX_PROCS" -le 0 ] && MAX_PROCS=1
+  fi
+fi
+
+check() {
+  label="$1"; dir="$2"; ext="$3"; parser="$4"
+  results=$(find "$dir" -name "*.$ext" -print0 | \
+    xargs -0 -P "$MAX_PROCS" -I {} sh -c "
+      if \"$parser\" -s 4000 \"\$1\" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+        echo 0
+      else
+        echo 1
+      fi
+    " _ {})
+  ok=$(printf '%s\n' "$results" | grep -c '^0$' || true)
+  fail=$(printf '%s\n' "$results" | grep -c '^1$' || true)
+  printf "  %-20s OK: %d  FAIL: %d\n" "$label" "$ok" "$fail"
+}
+
+echo "CPU limit: $MAX_PROCS threads"
+echo ""
+echo "Checking TXL parse compatibility..."
+echo "----------------------------------------"
+check "jnorm-soot"       /app/work/jnorm-soot       jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+check "jnorm-soot-agg"   /app/work/jnorm-soot-agg   jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+check "jnorm-sootup"     /app/work/jnorm-sootup     jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+check "jnorm-sootup-agg" /app/work/jnorm-sootup-agg jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+check "onorm"            /app/work/onorm            tac    "$TAC_PARSER"
+check "onorm-agg"        /app/work/onorm-agg        tac    "$TAC_PARSER"
+check "source"           /app/work/source           java   "$JAVA_PARSER"
+echo "----------------------------------------"
\ No newline at end of file

+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Logs TXL parsing failures for jnorm-soot, jnorm-soot-agg, jnorm-sootup, jnorm-sootup-agg, onorm, onorm-agg and source.
+# Run inside the Docker container. Output: /app/work/txl-parsing-failures/<label>.log
+set -eu
+
+JIMPLE_PARSER="/usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/jimple-extract-functions.x"
+TAC_PARSER="/usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/tac-extract-functions.x"
+JAVA_PARSER="/usr/local/lib/nicad/txl/java-extract-functions.x"
+OUT_DIR="/app/work/txl-parsing-failures"
+
+if [ ! -f /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max ]; then
+  MAX_PROCS=$(nproc)
+else
+  QUOTA=$(awk '{print $1}' /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max)
+  PERIOD=$(awk '{print $2}' /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max)
+  if [ "$QUOTA" = "max" ]; then
+    MAX_PROCS=$(nproc)
+  else
+    MAX_PROCS=$(( QUOTA / PERIOD ))
+    [ "$MAX_PROCS" -le 0 ] && MAX_PROCS=1
+  fi
+fi
+
+mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
+
+collectFailures() {
+  label="$1"; dir="$2"; ext="$3"; parser="$4"
+  log="$OUT_DIR/${label}.log"
+
+  bad=$(find "$dir" -name "*.$ext" -print0 | \
+    xargs -0 -P "$MAX_PROCS" -I {} sh -c "
+      \"$parser\" -s 4000 \"\$1\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo \"\$1\"
+    " _ {} | sort)
+
+  n=$(printf '%s\n' "$bad" | grep -c . || true)
+  printf "  %-20s FAIL: %d  -> %s\n" "$label" "$n" "$log"
+
+  {
+    echo "=== $label: $n failures ==="
+    echo ""
+    printf '%s\n' "$bad" | while IFS= read -r f; do
+      [ -z "$f" ] && continue
+      echo "=== $f ==="
+      "$parser" -s 4000 "$f" 2>&1 | head -8
+      echo "--- content (first 40 lines) ---"
+      head -40 "$f"
+      echo ""
+    done
+  } > "$log"
+}
+
+echo "CPU limit: $MAX_PROCS threads"
+echo ""
+echo "Collecting TXL parsing failures..."
+echo "----------------------------------------"
+collectFailures "jnorm-soot"       /app/work/jnorm-soot       jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+collectFailures "jnorm-soot-agg"   /app/work/jnorm-soot-agg   jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+collectFailures "jnorm-sootup"     /app/work/jnorm-sootup     jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+collectFailures "jnorm-sootup-agg" /app/work/jnorm-sootup-agg jimple "$JIMPLE_PARSER"
+collectFailures "onorm"            /app/work/onorm            tac    "$TAC_PARSER"
+collectFailures "onorm-agg"        /app/work/onorm-agg        tac    "$TAC_PARSER"
+collectFailures "source"           /app/work/source           java   "$JAVA_PARSER"
+echo "----------------------------------------"
\ No newline at end of file

+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Download the three data files required to run the pipeline.
+# Each file is verified against a known SHA-256 checksum to ensure integrity. If a file already exists, it will be skipped.
+# For OneDrive, the code snippet is based on https://github.com/eugenenuke/onedrive-downloader.git.
+#
+# - Cleaned StubFile BigCloneBench H2 database (Google Drive, ~600 MB)
+# - StubFiles (Google Drive, ~1000 MB)
+# - IJaDataset2.0 source fragments for BCE evaluation (OneDrive, ~100 MB)
+#
+# Requires: curl, sha256sum
+set -eu
+
+DATA="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/../data"
+mkdir -p "$DATA"
+
+if ! command -v curl > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "Error: curl is required but was not found. Please install curl and re-run this script." >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+download() {
+  name="$1"; url="$2"
+  dest="$DATA/$name"
+  if [ -f "$dest" ]; then
+    echo "  [skip] $name -- already downloaded"
+  else
+    echo "  [download] $name"
+    curl -L --progress-bar --fail -o "$dest" "$url" || {
+      rm -f "$dest"
+      echo "Error: download failed for $name." >&2
+      exit 1
+    }
+  fi
+}
+
+SHA256_BCB="3f4f720f89c852e01acc395d9fdddcb91a0490a3ef15a31342b90e55b1b8933e"
+SHA256_STUB="f686a0e65cd5e66cc399cbc0e0b6d6d3dc8a94ee92c73dcd97d0dee5a8ab2989"
+SHA256_IJA="61507bf31a082972e78fac11347ecff9af9c514adb77d6f63d12a0223c243b9d"
+
+verify() {
+  name="$1"; expected="$2"
+  dest="$DATA/$name"
+  if command -v sha256sum > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+    actual=$(sha256sum "$dest" | awk '{print $1}')
+  else
+    actual=$(shasum -a 256 "$dest" | awk '{print $1}')
+  fi
+  if [ "$actual" = "$expected" ]; then
+    echo "  [ok] $name checksum verified"
+  else
+    echo "Error: checksum mismatch for $name" >&2
+    echo "  expected: $expected" >&2
+    echo "  actual:   $actual" >&2
+    rm -f "$dest"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+}
+
+echo "Downloading files into data/ ..."
+echo ""
+
+# BigCloneBench H2 database
+download "bcb.h2.db.zip" \
+  "https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=1c95ubC-UBCAU0rudj6_UWSaE926qPxq_&export=download&confirm=t"
+verify "bcb.h2.db.zip" "$SHA256_BCB"
+
+# StubFiles
+download "StubFiles.zip" \
+  "https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=1-tjdLO3LUny1Kv6Nd1wHpiaXrK45_IPA&export=download&confirm=t"
+verify "StubFiles.zip" "$SHA256_STUB"
+
+# IJaDataset source fragments for BCE evaluation
+# OneDrive requires a Badger token to access public shares
+ONEDRIVE_FILE="IJaDataset_BCEvalVersion.tar.gz"
+ONEDRIVE_DEST="$DATA/$ONEDRIVE_FILE"
+if [ -f "$ONEDRIVE_DEST" ]; then
+  echo "  [skip] $ONEDRIVE_FILE -- already downloaded"
+else
+  echo "  [download] $ONEDRIVE_FILE"
+  ONEDRIVE_URL="https://1drv.ms/u/s!AhXbM6MKt_yLj_N15CewgjM7Y8NLKA?e=cScoRJ"
+  ENCODED=$(printf '%s' "$ONEDRIVE_URL" | base64 | tr -d '\n=' | tr '+/' '-_')
+  BADGER_TOKEN=$(curl -s --fail \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{"appId":"5cbed6ac-a083-4e14-b191-b4ba07653de2"}' \
+    "https://api-badgerp.svc.ms/v1.0/token" \
+    | grep -oP '"token":"\K[^"]+')
+  if [ -z "$BADGER_TOKEN" ]; then
+    echo "Error: could not obtain OneDrive Badger token." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  DOWNLOAD_URL=$(curl -s --fail \
+    -H "Accept: application/json" \
+    -H "Prefer: autoredeem" \
+    -H "Authorization: Badger $BADGER_TOKEN" \
+    -d '' \
+    "https://my.microsoftpersonalcontent.com/_api/v2.0/shares/u!${ENCODED}/driveitem?select=@content.downloadUrl,name" \
+    | grep -oP '"@content\.downloadUrl":"\K[^"]+')
+  if [ -z "$DOWNLOAD_URL" ]; then
+    echo "Error: could not resolve OneDrive download URL." >&2
+    exit 1
+  fi
+  curl -L --progress-bar --fail -o "$ONEDRIVE_DEST" "$DOWNLOAD_URL" || {
+    rm -f "$ONEDRIVE_DEST"
+    echo "Error: download failed for $ONEDRIVE_FILE." >&2
+    exit 1
+  }
+fi
+verify "$ONEDRIVE_FILE" "$SHA256_IJA"
+
+echo ""
+echo "All files are ready."
\ No newline at end of file

+#!/usr/bin/env sh
+# Sweep NiCad minsize over 6,10,15,20 with funcIds 6,10,11,12.
+# NiCad/mapping/eval re-run per value.
+# Cfg files are mounted over the baked-in image copies -- no rebuild needed.
+# Requires: docker compose build must have been run first.
+set -eu
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/.."
+CFGS="$ROOT/conf/nicad"
+
+set_minsize() {
+  for CFG in "$CFGS"/*.cfg; do
+    sed "s/^minsize=.*/minsize=$1/" "$CFG" > "$CFG.tmp" && mv "$CFG.tmp" "$CFG"
+  done
+}
+
+FIRST_RUN=true
+
+run() {
+  FORCE_ARG=""
+  if $FIRST_RUN; then
+    FORCE_ARG="--force"
+    FIRST_RUN=false
+  fi
+  docker compose -f "$ROOT/docker-compose.yml" run --rm \
+    -v "$CFGS/nicad-consistent.cfg:/usr/local/lib/nicad/config/nicad-consistent.cfg:ro" \
+    -v "$CFGS/nicad-blind.cfg:/usr/local/lib/nicad/config/nicad-blind.cfg:ro" \
+    -v "$CFGS/nicad-none.cfg:/usr/local/lib/nicad/config/nicad-none.cfg:ro" \
+    pipeline --func-ids "6,10,11,12" $FORCE_ARG
+}
+
+for N in 6 10 15 20; do
+  echo "=== minsize=$N ==="
+  [ -d "$ROOT/work/nicad_minsize_$N" ] && echo "  [skip]" && continue
+  set_minsize "$N"
+  run
+  for D in nicad mapping eval; do
+    [ -d "$ROOT/work/$D" ] && mv "$ROOT/work/$D" "$ROOT/work/${D}_minsize_$N"
+  done
+  [ -d "$ROOT/results/eval" ] && mv "$ROOT/results/eval" "$ROOT/results/eval_minsize_$N"
+done
+
+set_minsize 10
+echo "=== Restored minsize=10 ==="
+
+echo ""
+for N in 6 10 15 20; do
+  echo "--- minsize=$N ---"
+  for RENAMING in consistent blind none; do
+    F="$ROOT/results/eval_minsize_$N/$RENAMING/summary.txt"
+    [ -f "$F" ] && printf '[ %s ]\n' "$RENAMING" && cat "$F"
+  done
+done

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package cli
+
+import core.{formatDuration, Log, RunConfig, Slf4jOPALLogger}
+import core.Constants.*
+import mainargs.{arg, main, Flag, ParserForMethods}
+import org.opalj.log.{GlobalLogContext, OPALLogger}
+import steps.*
+
+/** Evaluation pipeline measuring code clone detection recall on BigCloneBench (IJaDataset2.0):
+  * generates JNorm IR, ONorm IR, and source code (the latter as baseline), runs NiCad clone
+  * detection on each, maps detected clones to BigCloneBench format, and measures recall via
+  * BigCloneEval.
+  *
+  * Entry point: parses CLI arguments and sequentially executes pipeline steps; all steps implement
+  * output caching and support safe resumption after interruption; all outputs are fully
+  * reproducible across runs.
+  */
+object Main:
+
+  @main
+  def run(
+      @arg(doc = "Comma-separated funcIds to process (default: all 43 funcIds)") funcIds: String =
+        "",
+      @arg(doc =
+        "Clear work/ and results/ before running (existing results are archived)"
+      ) force: Flag
+  ): Unit =
+    val activeIds =
+      if funcIds.isBlank then FULL_FUNC_IDS
+      else funcIds.split(',').map(_.trim.toInt).toSet
+
+    val unknown = activeIds -- FULL_FUNC_IDS
+    if unknown.nonEmpty then
+      sys.error(
+        s"Unknown funcIds: ${unknown.toSeq.sorted.mkString(",")}. Valid range: ${FULL_FUNC_IDS.toSeq.sorted.mkString(",")}."
+      )
+
+    val dataDir = appRoot / DATA_DIR_NAME
+    val workDir = appRoot / WORK_DIR_NAME
+    val resultsDir = appRoot / RESULTS_DIR_NAME
+
+    if force.value then
+      val prevSentinel = workDir / MODE_SENTINEL
+      if os.exists(prevSentinel) && os.exists(resultsDir) then
+        val prevIds = os.read(prevSentinel).trim
+        val archiveDir = resultsDir / RESULTS_ARCHIVE_DIR / prevIds
+        if os.exists(archiveDir) then os.remove.all(archiveDir)
+        os.makeDir.all(archiveDir)
+        os.list(resultsDir)
+          .filter(p => p.last != RESULTS_ARCHIVE_DIR && p.last != LOG_DIR_NAME)
+          .foreach(p => os.move(p, archiveDir / p.last))
+        Log.pipeline.info(s"[Force] Archived results -> results/archive/$prevIds/")
+      if os.exists(workDir) then os.list(workDir).foreach(os.remove.all)
+      if os.exists(resultsDir) then
+        os.list(resultsDir)
+          .filter(p => p.last != RESULTS_ARCHIVE_DIR && p.last != LOG_DIR_NAME)
+          .foreach(os.remove.all)
+      Log.pipeline.info("[Force] Cleared work/ and results/")
+
+    val sentinelValue = activeIds.toSeq.sorted.mkString("-")
+    val sentinel = workDir / MODE_SENTINEL
+    if os.exists(sentinel) then
+      val saved = os.read(sentinel).trim
+      if saved != sentinelValue then
+        sys.error(s"Previous run used funcIds [$saved]. Use --force to switch to [$sentinelValue].")
+
+    val config = RunConfig(
+      dataDir    = dataDir,
+      workDir    = workDir,
+      resultsDir = resultsDir,
+      funcIds    = activeIds
+    )
+
+    os.makeDir.all(workDir)
+    os.write.over(sentinel, sentinelValue)
+
+    val pipelineStart = System.currentTimeMillis()
+    Seq(
+      ExtractStep(),
+      CompileStep(),
+      ExtractSourceStep(),
+      JNormStep(),
+      ONormStep(),
+      CollectMetadataStep(),
+      NiCadStep(),
+      MapClonesStep(),
+      EvaluateStep()
+    ).foreach(_.execute(config))
+    val elapsed = formatDuration(System.currentTimeMillis() - pipelineStart)
+    Log.pipeline.info(s"Pipeline complete in $elapsed")
+    Log.metrics.info(s"Pipeline complete in $elapsed")
+
+  def main(args: Array[String]): Unit =
+    val runTs = java.time.LocalDateTime.now()
+      .format(java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss"))
+    val logDir = appRoot / RESULTS_DIR_NAME / LOG_DIR_NAME / runTs
+    os.makeDir.all(logDir)
+    System.setProperty("logDir", logDir.toString)
+    OPALLogger.updateLogger(GlobalLogContext, new Slf4jOPALLogger())
+    ParserForMethods(this).runOrExit(args.toIndexedSeq): Unit

+package io.github.lukawnb

+
+def formatDuration(millis: Long): String =
+  val d = JDuration.ofMillis(millis)
+  val hours = d.toHours
+  val minutes = d.toMinutesPart
+  val seconds = d.toSecondsPart
+  val parts = List(
+    Option.when(hours > 0)(s"${hours}h"),
+    Option.when(hours > 0 || minutes > 0)(s"${minutes}m"),
+    Some(s"${seconds}s")
+  ).flatten
+  parts.mkString(" ")

+  val evalWorkDir: Path = workDir / EVAL_WORK_DIR
+  val evalResultsDir: Path = resultsDir / EVAL_WORK_DIR
+
+  def isIncomplete(outDir: os.Path): Boolean =
+    ALL_TARGETS.exists(t => funcIds.exists(id => !os.exists(outDir / t / id.toString)))
+
+extension (dir: os.Path)(using config: RunConfig)
+  def funcIdSubDirs: IndexedSeq[os.Path] =
+    os.list(dir).filter(p => os.isDir(p) && p.last.toIntOption.exists(config.funcIds.contains))
+
+extension (dir: os.Path)
+  def categorySubDirs: IndexedSeq[os.Path] =
+    os.list(dir).filter(p => os.isDir(p) && CATEGORIES.contains(p.last))
+
+  def fragmentSubDirs: IndexedSeq[os.Path] =
+    os.list(dir).filter(p => os.isDir(p) && p.last.startsWith("_"))
+
+extension (path: os.Path)
+  def writeZstd(body: ZstdOutputStream => Unit): Unit =
+    val tmp = path / os.up / (path.last + ".tmp")
+    val out = new ZstdOutputStream(
+      new java.io.BufferedOutputStream(java.nio.file.Files.newOutputStream(tmp.toNIO))
+    )
+    try
+      body(out)
+      out.close()
+      os.move(tmp, path, replaceExisting = true)
+    catch
+      case e: Throwable =>
+        try out.close()
+        catch case _ => ()
+        try os.remove(tmp)
+        catch case _ => ()
+        throw e
+
+  def readZstd[A](body: java.io.InputStream => A): A =
+    val in = new com.github.luben.zstd.ZstdInputStream(
+      new java.io.BufferedInputStream(java.nio.file.Files.newInputStream(path.toNIO))
+    )
+    try body(in)
+    finally in.close()

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package core
+
+import java.util.concurrent.{ConcurrentLinkedQueue, Executors, Semaphore}
+import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger
+import scala.concurrent.{Await, ExecutionContext, Future}
+import scala.concurrent.duration.Duration
+import scala.util.Using
+
+import org.slf4j.MDC
+
+val CPU = Runtime.getRuntime.availableProcessors()
+
+trait Step:
+  def name: String
+
+  def process(using RunConfig): Unit
+
+  final def execute(config: RunConfig): Unit =
+    given RunConfig = config
+    MDC.put("step", name)
+    Slf4jOPALLogger.currentStep = name
+    val start = System.currentTimeMillis()
+    Log.pipeline.info("========================================")
+    Log.pipeline.info(s"==> Start Step: $name")
+    try
+      process
+      val duration = formatDuration(System.currentTimeMillis() - start)
+      Log.pipeline.info(s"==> Done: $name in $duration\n")
+      Log.metrics.info(s"STEP\t$name\t$duration\n")
+      Log.jnorm.info("\n")
+      Log.opal.warn("\n")
+      Log.nicad.info("\n")
+      Log.bce.info("\n")
+    catch
+      case t: Throwable =>
+        Log.pipeline.error(s"!!! ERROR in $name: ${t.getMessage}")
+        throw t
+    finally
+      Slf4jOPALLogger.currentStep = "-"
+      MDC.remove("step")
+
+final def runParallel[T](label: String, items: Seq[T], permits: Int = CPU)(f: T => Unit): Unit =
+  if items.isEmpty then return
+  val sem = Option.when(permits > 0)(new Semaphore(permits))
+  val failures = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue[Throwable]()
+  val counter = new AtomicInteger(0)
+  val lastPrint = new java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong(0L)
+  val total = items.size
+  val parentMdc = Option(MDC.getCopyOfContextMap)
+
+  Using.resource(Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()): executor =>
+    given ExecutionContext = ExecutionContext.fromExecutor(executor)
+    val tasks = items.map: item =>
+      Future:
+        parentMdc.foreach(MDC.setContextMap)
+        sem.foreach(_.acquire())
+        try f(item)
+        catch case t: Throwable => failures.add(t)
+        finally sem.foreach(_.release())
+        val current = counter.incrementAndGet()
+        val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
+        val last = lastPrint.get()
+        if (now - last >= 1000 && lastPrint.compareAndSet(last, now)) || current == total then
+          val pct = (current * 100) / total
+          val bar = "=" * (pct / 5) + " " * (20 - pct / 5)
+          print(s"\r  [$label] $pct% [$bar] ($current/$total)")
+          System.out.flush()
+    Await.result(Future.sequence(tasks), Duration.Inf)
+    println()
+
+  if !failures.isEmpty then
+    failures.forEach(e => Log.pipeline.error(s"[$label] Task failed: ${e.getMessage}", e))
+    val first = failures.peek()
+    throw RuntimeException(s"[$label] ${failures.size} task(s) failed", first)

+  // Uniform distribution across java targets 8/11/17 via a deterministic seed-42 sorted shuffle.
+  private def constructCrossMapping(target8Dir: os.Path)
+      : List[(relPath: os.RelPath, version: Int)] =
+    val rng = new Random(SEED)
+    val versions = Vector(8, 11, 17)
+

+      .flatMap(funcDir => funcDir.categorySubDirs)

+      .toVector
+
+    val shuffled = rng.shuffle(fragDirs.sortBy(_.toString))
+    shuffled.zipWithIndex.map((p, i) => (relPath = p, version = versions(i % versions.size))).toList
+
+  private def copyFragmentToTargetCross(
+      fragRelPath: os.RelPath,
+      version: Int,
+      baseDir: os.Path,
+      fileExtension: String

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package core.utils
+
+object HeapCalculator:
+
+  private val PIPELINE_RESERVE_MB = 1024L
+  private val PER_JVM_NATIVE_MB = 192L
+  private val MIN_HEAP_MB = 512
+
+  private val availableMb: Long =
+    import java.lang.management.ManagementFactory
+    val totalMb = ManagementFactory.getOperatingSystemMXBean match
+      case bean: com.sun.management.OperatingSystemMXBean =>
+        bean.getTotalMemorySize / (1L << 20)
+      case _                                              => 8192L
+    (totalMb - PIPELINE_RESERVE_MB).max(0L)
+
+  // Heap per JVM when parallelism processes run concurrently.
+  def perProcessMb(parallelism: Int): Int =
+    (availableMb / parallelism.max(1) - PER_JVM_NATIVE_MB).toInt.max(MIN_HEAP_MB)
+
+  // Heap for a single bulk/retry process using fraction of available RAM.
+  def bulkMb(fraction: Double =
+    0.85): Int = (availableMb * fraction - PER_JVM_NATIVE_MB).toInt.max(MIN_HEAP_MB)

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package core.utils
+
+import scala.collection.mutable
+
+object IrMethodParser:
+
+  // Jimple has a class wrapper -> methods at brace depth 1, bodies at depth 2.
+  // TAC has no class wrapper   -> methods at brace depth 0, bodies at depth 1.
+  def parseJimple(file: os.Path): Map[String, (start: Int, end: Int)] = parse(file, baseDepth = 1)
+  def parseTac(file: os.Path): Map[String, (start: Int, end: Int)] = parse(file, baseDepth = 0)
+
+  private def parse(irFile: os.Path, baseDepth: Int): Map[String, (start: Int, end: Int)] =
+    val lines = os.read.lines(irFile)
+    val result = mutable.Map[String, (start: Int, end: Int)]()
+    var depth = 0
+    var pendingMethod: Option[(name: String, startLine: Int)] = None
+
+    lines.zipWithIndex.foreach: (rawLine, idx) =>
+      val lineNum = idx + 1
+      val line = rawLine.trim
+      val prevDepth = depth
+      depth += rawLine.count(_ == '{') - rawLine.count(_ == '}')
+
+      if prevDepth == baseDepth && line.contains("(") && !line.endsWith(";") then
+        val name = line.substring(0, line.indexOf('(')).trim.split("\\s+").last
+        pendingMethod = Some((name = name, startLine = lineNum))
+
+      if prevDepth == baseDepth + 1 && depth == baseDepth then
+        pendingMethod.foreach: m =>
+          result(m.name) = (start = m.startLine, end = lineNum)
+        pendingMethod = None
+
+    result.toMap

+
+case class LargeMethod(
+    funcId: Int,
+    category: String,
+    fragment: String,
+    className: String,
+    kb: Long,
+    maxInstr: Int
+)
+
+object ScanLargeMethods:
+
+  private val THRESHOLD = 5_000
+
+  private val targetFrameworks = List(
+    TARGET_8  -> ((dis: DataInputStream) => Java8Framework.ClassFile(dis)),
+    TARGET_11 -> ((dis: DataInputStream) => Java11Framework.ClassFile(dis)),
+    TARGET_17 -> ((dis: DataInputStream) => Java17Framework.ClassFile(dis))
+  )
+
+  def scan(compileDir: os.Path)(using RunConfig): List[LargeMethod] =
+    val results = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue[LargeMethod]()
+    val failures = new AtomicInteger(0)
+
+    for (targetName, readClassFile) <- targetFrameworks do
+      val scanDir = compileDir / targetName
+      if !os.exists(scanDir) then
+        Log.pipeline.info(s"  [Skip] $targetName not present, skipping scan.")
+      else
+        val classFiles =
+          for
+            funcDir     <- scanDir.funcIdSubDirs
+            categoryDir <- funcDir.categorySubDirs
+            fragmentDir <- os.list(categoryDir)
+            classFile   <- os.list(fragmentDir) if classFile.ext == CLASS_EXT
+          yield classFile
+
+        Log.pipeline.info(
+          s"  [Scan] $targetName: ${classFiles.size} class files (THRESHOLD=$THRESHOLD)"
+        )
+
+        runParallel(s"Scan $targetName", classFiles, CPU): classFile =>
+          try
+            val maxInstr =
+              readClassFile(new DataInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(os.read.bytes(classFile))))
+                .headOption
+                .flatMap(cf => cf.methods.flatMap(_.body).map(_.instructionsCount).maxOption)
+                .getOrElse(0)
+
+            if maxInstr >= THRESHOLD then
+              classFile.relativeTo(scanDir).segments match
+                case Seq(funcId, category, fragment, _) =>
+                  results.add(LargeMethod(
+                    funcId.toInt,
+                    category,
+                    fragment,
+                    classFile.last,
+                    os.size(classFile) / 1024,
+                    maxInstr
+                  )): Unit
+                case _                                  => ()
+          catch
+            case e: Exception =>
+              failures.incrementAndGet()
+              Log.pipeline.error(s"  [ParseError] $classFile: ${e.getMessage}")
+
+    if failures.get() > 0 then
+      Log.pipeline.warn(
+        s"  [Warn] ${failures.get()} class file(s) could not be parsed -- coverage may be incomplete"
+      )
+
+    results.asScala.toSeq
+      .groupBy(m => (m.funcId, m.category, m.fragment, m.className))
+      .values
+      .map(_.maxBy(_.maxInstr))
+      .toList
+      .sortBy(m => (m.funcId, m.category, m.fragment, m.className))

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package onorm
+
+import java.net.URL
+

+import onorm.core.OptimizationPass.optimize
+import onorm.core.TacMethod
+import onorm.passes.normalization.{StringConcatNormalizer, TypecheckNormalizer}
+import onorm.passes.optimization.{
+  CopyConstantPropagator,
+  DeadAssignmentEliminator,
+  UnconditionalBranchFolder,
+  UnreachableCodeEliminator
+}
+import onorm.postprocess.TacRenderer
+import onorm.preprocess.{SyntheticClassFilter, SyntheticMethodFilter}
+import org.opalj.br.analyses.Project
+import org.opalj.tac.TACAI
+
+/** ONorm lifts Java bytecode (class files) into a Three-Address Code (TAC/SSA) intermediate
+  * representation derived via OPAL's abstract interpretation. Inspired by JNorm (Schott et al.,
+  * ECOOP 2024), it applies 8 baseline optimizations:
+  *   - copy propagation
+  *   - constant propagation and folding
+  *   - dead assignment elimination
+  *   - conditional branch folding (via OPAL's L1 abstract interpretation)
+  *   - unconditional branch folding (for N12 retargeting)
+  *   - unreachable code elimination (as safety net)
+  *   - null check elimination (via OPAL's L1 abstract interpretation)
+  *   - unused local elimination (in SSA collapses with dead assignment elimination)
+  * and the 4 most prevalent normalizations identified per JNorm's prevalence analysis to reduce
+  * compiler-induced differences between Java versions:
+  *   - N1: synthetic method elimination; extended to synthetic class files - OPAL's
+  *     InvokedynamicRewriting materialises lambda proxy classes for call-graph analysis that are
+  *     absent from the original bytecode and invalid as TXL identifiers
+  *   - N12: dynamic string concatenation normalization
+  *   - N14: private method invocation normalization
+  *   - N16: typecheck normalization (aggressive mode only)
+  *
+  * Entry point: orchestrates preprocessing -> TAC/SSA generation -> normalization -> optimization
+  * -> rendering; each stage is implemented by the respective pass or filter. Passes share state via
+  * TacMethod's patch overlay. Pass order is fixed by inter-pass dependencies (N12 before UBF, CCP
+  * and UCE before DAE).
+  */
+object ONorm:
+
+  def run(fragmentDir: os.Path, outputDir: os.Path, aggressive: Boolean = false): Unit =
+    val fragmentId = fragmentDir.last
+    given project: Project[URL] = Project(fragmentDir.toIO)
+    project.projectClassFilesWithSources.map(_._1).filter(SyntheticClassFilter).foreach:
+      classFile =>
+        val methods = classFile.methods
+          .filter(SyntheticMethodFilter)                // N1
+          .flatMap: method =>
+            try Some(TacMethod(method, TACAI(project, method)().detach()))
+            catch
+              case e: Exception =>
+                io.github.lukawnb.core.Log.pipeline.error(
+                  s"  [ONorm] ${classFile.thisType.toJava}.${method.name}: ${e.getMessage}"
+                )
+                None
+          .normalize(StringConcatNormalizer)            // N12
+          .normalizeIf(aggressive)(TypecheckNormalizer) // N16 (aggressive mode only)
+          .optimize(CopyConstantPropagator)
+          .optimize(UnconditionalBranchFolder)
+          .optimize(UnreachableCodeEliminator)
+          .optimize(DeadAssignmentEliminator)
+        val content = TacRenderer.renderClass(methods)  // N14
+        if content.nonEmpty then
+          val outFile = outputDir / fragmentId / s"${classFile.thisType.simpleName}.tac"
+          os.makeDir.all(outFile / os.up)
+          os.write.over(outFile, content)

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package onorm.passes.normalization
+
+import onorm.core.*
+import org.opalj.br.{ClassType, ReferenceType}
+
+given CanEqual[ReferenceType, ClassType] = CanEqual.derived
+import java.net.URL
+import scala.collection.mutable
+import scala.util.boundary
+import scala.util.boundary.break
+
+import org.opalj.br.analyses.Project
+import org.opalj.br.instructions.LDCString
+import org.opalj.tac.*
+import org.opalj.value.ValueInformation
+
+/** N12 -- normalizes dynamic string concatenation across JDK versions.
+  *
+  *   1. Scans all statements for Pattern A (>=JDK 9) or Pattern B (<=JDK 8).
+  *   2. For each match: emits StmtPatch.Concat(parts) at the call site and StmtPatch.Drop for all
+  *      consumed chain statements; ConcatPart.Arg holds the original OPAL Expr (not rendered text).
+  *
+  * Pattern A (>=JDK 9 -- invokedynamic): OPAL's InvokedynamicRewriting rewrites StringConcatFactory
+  * invokedynamics as StaticFunctionCalls to private synthetic $string_concat$... proxies; the proxy
+  * bytecode holds a single LDC recipe string where Slot marks dynamic-argument slots and Tag marks
+  * static constants (unsupported -- falls back to call-as-is). Splits the recipe on Slot and
+  * interleaves literal segments with Arg(param) slots.
+  *
+  * Pattern B (<=JDK 8 -- StringBuilder chain): traces backward from the toString() receiver through
+  * single-def definedBy links, collecting each append argument and the optional reference-typed
+  * <init> argument. Bails conservatively on multi-def receivers or unexpected nodes.
+  */
+private[onorm] object StringConcatNormalizer extends NormalizationPass:
+
+  private val ProxyPrefix = "$string_concat$"
+  private val Slot = 1.toChar.toString
+  private val Tag = 2.toChar.toString // OPAL's Tag slot in the recipe -- static constant
+
+  override def apply(tacMethod: TacMethod)(using project: Project[URL]): TacMethod =
+    var patches = tacMethod.patches
+    val stmts = tacMethod.tac.stmts
+    var i = 0
+    while i < stmts.length do
+      patchAt(i, tacMethod) match
+        case Some((concatIdx, parts, drops)) =>
+          patches = patches.updated(StmtIndex(concatIdx), StmtPatch.Concat(parts))
+          drops.foreach: d =>
+            if d != concatIdx && !patches.contains(StmtIndex(d)) then
+              patches = patches.updated(StmtIndex(d), StmtPatch.Drop)
+        case None                            => ()
+      i += 1
+    tacMethod.copy(patches = patches)
+
+  private def patchAt(
+      i: Int,
+      tacMethod: TacMethod
+  )(using
+      project: Project[URL]
+  ): Option[(concatIdx: Int, parts: Seq[ConcatPart], drops: Set[Int])] =
+    callAt(tacMethod.tac.stmts(i)).flatMap:
+      case sc: StaticFunctionCall[DUVar[ValueInformation]] @unchecked
+          if sc.name.startsWith(ProxyPrefix) =>
+        recipeParts(sc).map(p => (concatIdx = i, parts = p, drops = Set(i)))
+      case vfc: VirtualFunctionCall[DUVar[ValueInformation]] @unchecked
+          if vfc.name == "toString" && isStringBuilderLike(vfc.declaringClass) =>
+        traceAppendChain(vfc.receiver, tacMethod).map(r =>
+          (concatIdx = i, parts = r.parts, drops = r.drops + i)
+        )
+      case _ => None
+
+  private def callAt(
+      stmt: Stmt[DUVar[ValueInformation]]
+  ): Option[Expr[DUVar[ValueInformation]]] = stmt match
+    case Assignment(_, _, e) => Some(e)
+    case ExprStmt(_, e)      => Some(e)
+    case _                   => None
+
+  private def recipeParts(
+      sc: StaticFunctionCall[DUVar[ValueInformation]]
+  )(using project: Project[URL]): Option[Seq[ConcatPart]] =
+    val proxy = project.classFile(sc.declaringClass).flatMap(_.findMethod(sc.name, sc.descriptor))
+    val recipe = proxy
+      .flatMap(_.body)
+      .flatMap: code =>
+        code.instructions.iterator.filter(_ != null).collectFirst:
+          case LDCString(s) => s
+      .getOrElse(Slot * sc.params.size) // pure-dynamic: one empty slot per param
+    if recipe.contains(Tag) then None   // rare static-constant slot -- fall back to call as-is
+    else
+      val segments = recipe.split(Slot, -1) // -1 keeps trailing empty segments
+      val parts = mutable.ListBuffer.empty[ConcatPart]
+      var k = 0
+      while k < segments.length do
+        if segments(k).nonEmpty then parts += ConcatPart.Literal(segments(k))
+        if k < sc.params.size then parts += ConcatPart.Arg(sc.params(k))
+        k += 1
+      Some(parts.toSeq)
+
+  private def traceAppendChain(
+      toStringReceiver: Expr[DUVar[ValueInformation]],
+      tacMethod: TacMethod
+  ): Option[(parts: Seq[ConcatPart], drops: Set[Int])] =

+package io.github.lukawnb
+package onorm.passes.optimization

+import java.net.URL

+/** Mark-and-sweep dead code elimination (Cytron et al., "Efficiently Computing Static Single
+  * Assignment Form and the Control Dependence Graph", 1991, 7.1 Dead Code Elimination Fig. 17).
+  *
+  * A statement S is live under three conditions (Fig. 17): (1) S has observable side effects, (2) a
+  * live statement uses a value defined by S (Definers(S) backward closure), (3) S is a conditional
+  * branch control-dependent on a live statement (CD^(-1)(Block(S))).
+  *
+  * ONorm implements (1) and (2); condition (3) is omitted: OPAL's abstract interpretation already
+  * folds dead branches at AITACode construction time, and JNorm (Schott et al., ECOOP 2024) omits
+  * CD as well -- parity ensures recall differences between ONorm and JNorm are attributable to
+  * ONorm's normalizations, not to a stronger elimination criterion. CD^(-1) would increase recall
+  * of semantically equivalent clones (Type 4) but is out of scope for a JNorm-comparable
+  * evaluation.
+  *
+  *   1. Mark: seeds live and worklist with every PreLive statement -- !isSideEffectFree (condition
+  *      1); If/Goto/Switch explicitly (all three have isSideEffectFree == true); Concat patches
+  *      (effective() returns Opaque -- side-effect freedom untestable). Propagates via (2):
+  *      single-def UVar uses follow the resolved map (Alias chains to real def-site; Const
+  *      short-circuits); multi-def uses (PHIs) mark all def-sites live.
+  *   2. Sweep: every non-live, side-effect-free, unpatched statement is Dropped.
+  *
+  * followResolved extends Definers(S) with CCP's resolved map: Alias entries chain through without
+  * marking the copy live; Const entries short-circuit -- achieving CCP+DCE without mutation of the
+  * immutable AITACode.
+  */
+private[onorm] object DeadAssignmentEliminator extends OptimizationPass:
+
+  override def apply(tacMethod: TacMethod)(using project: Project[URL]): TacMethod =
+    val length = tacMethod.tac.stmts.length
+    if length == 0 then return tacMethod
+
+    // Phase 1 -- Mark.
+    var live = IntTrieSet.empty
+    val worklist = mutable.ArrayDeque.empty[Int]
+    var i = 0
+    while i < length do
+      if isCritical(i, tacMethod) then
+        live += i
+        worklist.append(i)
+      i += 1
+    while worklist.nonEmpty do
+      val idx = worklist.removeHead()
+      usesAt(idx, tacMethod).foreach: u =>
+        val defs = u.definedBy
+        if defs.size == 1 then live = followResolved(defs.head, tacMethod, live, worklist)
+        else
+          defs.foreach: d =>
+            if d >= 0 && !live.contains(d) then
+              live += d
+              worklist.append(d)
+
+    // Phase 2 -- Sweep.
+    var patches = tacMethod.patches
+    i = 0
+    while i < length do
+      val si = StmtIndex(i)
+      if !live.contains(i) then
+        tacMethod.effective(si) match
+          case StmtView.Stmt(s) if s.isSideEffectFree && !patches.contains(si) =>
+            patches = patches.updated(si, StmtPatch.Drop)
+          case _                                                               => ()
+      i += 1
+    tacMethod.copy(patches = patches)
+
+  private def isCritical(i: Int, tacMethod: TacMethod): Boolean =
+    tacMethod.effective(StmtIndex(i)) match
+      case StmtView.Stmt(_: If[?])     => true
+      case StmtView.Stmt(_: Goto)      => true
+      case StmtView.Stmt(_: Switch[?]) => true
+      case StmtView.Stmt(s)            => !s.isSideEffectFree
+      case StmtView.Opaque             => true
+      case StmtView.Dropped            => false
+
+  // Concat patches: must visit Arg(expr) -- otherwise concat arguments appear dead
+  // and their defining statements get swept, leaving a dangling lv<hex> in concat(...).
+  private def usesAt(i: Int, tacMethod: TacMethod): Iterator[UVar[ValueInformation]] =
+    tacMethod.patches.get(StmtIndex(i)) match
+      case Some(StmtPatch.Concat(parts)) =>
+        parts.iterator.flatMap:
+          case ConcatPart.Arg(expr) => collectUVars(expr)
+          case _                    => Iterator.empty
+      case Some(StmtPatch.Replace(s))    => uvarsInStmt(s)
+      case Some(StmtPatch.Drop)          => Iterator.empty
+      case None                          => uvarsInStmt(tacMethod.tac.stmts(i))
+
+  // Alias: follow chain to real def-site. Const: no def-site to mark live.
+  // Negative defSite: parameter or exception origin -- nothing to mark.
+  private def followResolved(
+      defSite: Int,
+      tacMethod: TacMethod,
+      live: IntTrieSet,
+      worklist: mutable.ArrayDeque[Int]
+  ): IntTrieSet =
+    if defSite < 0 then live
+    else
+      var lv = live
+      var d = defSite
+      var seen = IntTrieSet.empty
+      boundary:
+        while !seen.contains(d) do
+          seen += d
+          tacMethod.resolved.get(StmtIndex(d)) match
+            case Some(RValue.Alias(d2)) =>
+              if d2 < 0 then break() else d = d2
+            case Some(RValue.Const(_))  => break()
+            case None                   =>
+              if !lv.contains(d) then
+                lv += d
+                worklist.append(d)
+              break()
+      lv
+
+  // forallSubExpressions skips Assignment.targetVar (LHS DVar is a definition, not a use).
+  private def uvarsInStmt(stmt: Stmt[DUVar[ValueInformation]]): Iterator[UVar[ValueInformation]] =
+    gatherUVars(stmt.forallSubExpressions[DUVar[ValueInformation]])
+
+  private def collectUVars(
+      expr: Expr[DUVar[ValueInformation]]
+  ): Iterator[UVar[ValueInformation]] =
+    expr match
+      case u: UVar[?] => Iterator.single(u.asInstanceOf[UVar[ValueInformation]])
+      case _          => gatherUVars(expr.forallSubExpressions[DUVar[ValueInformation]])
+
+  private def gatherUVars(
+      forall: (Expr[DUVar[ValueInformation]] => Boolean) => Boolean
+  ): Iterator[UVar[ValueInformation]] =
+    val buf = mutable.ListBuffer.empty[UVar[ValueInformation]]
+    forall: e =>
+      buf ++= collectUVars(e)
+      true
+    buf.iterator

+/** Jump threading (Aho, Lam, Sethi, Ullman, "Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools", 2nd
+  * ed., Sec. 8.7.3 "Flow-of-Control Optimizations"; cf. LLVM JumpThreading pass).
+  *
+  * For every Goto and If, chases the target through Goto chains and Dropped fall-throughs (a
+  * Dropped statement falls through to i + 1), retargeting the branch via StmtPatch.Replace if the
+  * threaded index differs. Branch targets in the detached AITACode are already statement indices --
+  * no PC-to-index conversion needed.
+  *
+  * Goto->Goto chains are a safety net -- OPAL pre-resolves them at TAC construction. The only case
+  * in which threading takes effect: any If or Goto targeting a JDK 8 StringBuilder chain dropped by
+  * N12.
+  *
+  * Switch targets are not threaded: TacRenderer.forward() covers them at render time (Step 6). UCE
+  * and DAE are entirely independent of UBF retargeting: UCE's BFS follows Dropped fall-throughs,
+  * DAE performs only def-use analysis.
+  */
+private[onorm] object UnconditionalBranchFolder extends OptimizationPass:
+
+  override def apply(tacMethod: TacMethod)(using project: Project[URL]): TacMethod =
+    var patches = tacMethod.patches
+    val stmts = tacMethod.tac.stmts
+    var i = 0
+    while i < stmts.length do
+      tacMethod.effective(StmtIndex(i)) match
+        case StmtView.Stmt(g: Goto)  =>
+          val threaded = thread(g.targetStmt, tacMethod)
+          if threaded != g.targetStmt then
+            patches = patches.updated(StmtIndex(i), StmtPatch.Replace(Goto(g.pc, threaded)))
+        case StmtView.Stmt(f: If[?]) =>
+          val threaded = thread(f.targetStmt, tacMethod)
+          if threaded != f.targetStmt then
+            patches = patches.updated(
+              StmtIndex(i),
+              StmtPatch.Replace(If(f.pc, f.left, f.condition, f.right, threaded))
+            )
+        case _                       => ()
+      i += 1
+    tacMethod.copy(patches = patches)
+
+  // cycle-safe: self-loop returns cycle entry; fall-through past end returns original target
+  private def thread(target: Int, tacMethod: TacMethod): Int =
+    val length = tacMethod.tac.stmts.length
+    var current = target
+    var seen = IntTrieSet.empty
+    boundary[Int]:
+      while !seen.contains(current) do
+        if current < 0 || current >= length then break(target)
+        seen += current
+        tacMethod.effective(StmtIndex(current)) match
+          case StmtView.Stmt(g: Goto) => current = g.targetStmt
+          case StmtView.Dropped       => current += 1
+          case _                      => break(current)
+      current

+  * statement 0.
+  *
+  * For directly javac-compiled .class files (IJaDataset 2.0), this pass is a provable no-op: the
+  * Java Language Specification (JLS) Sec. 14.21 rejects structurally unreachable statements at
+  * compile time (code after unconditional exits, while(false)/for(false) bodies); Sec. 14.21
+  * explicitly does not track expression values -- those cases are handled by OPAL's L1 domain at
+  * TAC construction. Javac folds compile-time constants (Sec. 15.28/Sec. 4.12.4). Neither N12 nor
+  * UBF produce new unreachable live statements: N12 emits only Drop/Replace patches and touches no
+  * branches, leaving live-stmt reachability unchanged; UBF's thread() traverses only Goto and
+  * Dropped stmts and stops at the first live stmt, so the retargeted branch lands on a stmt that
+  * was already transitively reachable. UCE is kept as a safety net for non-standard bytecode and
+  * defense-in-depth correctness.
+  *
+  * Exception-handler entry points are seeded into the BFS (handlerPC is a statement index after
+  * detach(), not a bytecode PC) so that catch blocks, which have no normal CFG predecessor, are not
+  * incorrectly dropped. Must run before DeadAssignmentEliminator: a use in unreachable code would
+  * otherwise keep its definition live.
+  */

+  override def apply(tacMethod: TacMethod)(using project: Project[URL]): TacMethod =
+    val length = tacMethod.tac.stmts.length
+    if length == 0 then return tacMethod
+    val worklist = mutable.ArrayDeque[Int](0)
+    tacMethod.tac.exceptionHandlers.foreach: eh =>
+      if eh.handlerPC >= 0 && eh.handlerPC < length then worklist.append(eh.handlerPC)
+    var reachable = IntTrieSet.empty
+    while worklist.nonEmpty do
+      val i = worklist.removeHead()
+      if !reachable.contains(i) then
+        reachable += i
+        successorsOf(i, tacMethod).foreach: s =>
+          if s >= 0 && s < length && !reachable.contains(s) then worklist.append(s)
+    var patches = tacMethod.patches
+    var i = 0
+    while i < length do
+      if !reachable.contains(i) && !patches.contains(StmtIndex(i)) then
+        patches = patches.updated(StmtIndex(i), StmtPatch.Drop)
+      i += 1
+    tacMethod.copy(patches = patches)
+
+  // control-flow successors of the effective statement at i
+  private def successorsOf(i: Int, tacMethod: TacMethod): Seq[Int] =
+    tacMethod.effective(StmtIndex(i)) match
+      case StmtView.Stmt(g: Goto)           => Seq(g.targetStmt)
+      case StmtView.Stmt(f: If[?])          => Seq(f.targetStmt, i + 1)
+      case StmtView.Stmt(sw: Switch[?])     => sw.defaultStmt +: sw.caseStmts

+      case StmtView.Stmt(_: ReturnValue[?]) => Seq.empty
+      case StmtView.Stmt(_: Throw[?])       => Seq.empty
+      case _                                => Seq(i + 1)
